post.post_content:
Black Friday 2026 is on 27 November, and Cyber Monday is on 30 November. Hostinger says Cyber Week falls inside its sale window. This page lists web hosting deals that we read on each host's own page. Seven hosts were read on 20 November 2026, and three on 15 or 16 November. Some deals end as early as 30 November, and one runs to 14 December. We did not test these hosts. Where a third party did, we name it in our reviews.

The picks are ordered by how clearly each host states its sale price, its term and its renewal price. They are not ranked by a test score. Offers change, so check the date and terms on the host's page before you pay.

Black Friday web hosting deals at a glance

HostThe dealEndsRenews atOur review
BluehostStarter $4.24 a month on a 12-month term30 Nov, 11:59 p.m. ET$13.79 a monthBluehost review
KinstaFirst month free, then 50% off for 3 months. New customers1 Dec$35 a month, no jumpKinsta review
ScalaHostingEntry Cloud $11.21 a month for 1 year. New plans1 Dec$39.95 a monthRead 15 Nov
InMotionUp to 75% off shared plans1 Dec, 12 p.m. ETLaunch $13.99 a monthRead 15 Nov
Cloudways80% off the first 2 months with code BFCM802. New accounts4 DecNo increaseCloudways review
NamecheapStellar $2.28 a month billed yearly. EasyWP Starter $1.48 a month4 Dec$55.88 a year (Stellar)Namecheap review
HostingerPremium $1.99 a month on a 48-month term. No code14 Dec$10.99 a monthHostinger review
hosting.comStarter $1.49 a month on a 12-month term. Applied automatically1 Dec or 14 Dec (two pages disagree)$13.99 a monthhosting.com review
DreamHostLaunch $2.89 a month on a 1-year termNo end date on the page$10.99 a monthDreamHost review

What does a Black Friday hosting deal really cost?

The big number on a sale banner is almost always a promo price for a long term. The price after that term is the real cost. This table shows what you pay at checkout and what the plan renews at. The totals are our own arithmetic from each host's prices.

Host and planPromo price a monthTermPaid at checkoutRenews at, a month
hosting.com Starter$1.4912 months$17.88$13.99
Namecheap EasyWP Starter$1.481 year$17.76$5.74 ($68.88 a year)
Hostinger Premium$1.9948 months$95.52$10.99
Namecheap Stellar$2.281 year$27.36$4.66 ($55.88 a year)
DreamHost Launch$2.891 year$34.68$10.99
Bluehost Starter$4.2412 months$50.88$13.79
Bluehost Starter$3.9936 months$143.64$11.49
ScalaHosting Entry Cloud$11.211 year$134.52$39.95
Cloudways Premium Micro$2.80 for 2 months, then $14Pay as you go$145.60 over the first year$14, no increase
Kinsta $35 plan$0, then $17.50 for 3 months, then $35Monthly$332.50 over the first year$35, no increase

Do the sums. hosting.com Starter renews at about 9.4 times its sale price, Hostinger Premium at about 5.5 times, and Bluehost Starter on a 12-month term at about 3.3 times. Cloudways and Kinsta do not raise the price at renewal, so the saving is only the first months. A deal is only a deal if you can live with the renewal price, or if you plan to move again.

When do the Black Friday hosting deals end?

  1. 30 November: Bluehost's 12-month offer ends at 11:59 p.m. Eastern time. Hosting.com says its deal prices run through Cyber Monday on 30 November.
  2. 1 December: Kinsta's first month free, ScalaHosting's cloud offer and InMotion's sale (12 p.m. Eastern time).
  3. 4 December: Cloudways code BFCM802 and Namecheap's Biggest Sale of the Year.
  4. 14 December: Hostinger's sale, which runs from 19 October.

Two hosting.com pages disagree on its end date. The Black Friday FAQ says 14 December, and the plan catalog says 1 December. Treat 1 December as the safe date.

1-year vs 3-year Black Friday deals: which saves more?

A longer term costs more at checkout and saves more over time, because the renewal is higher than the deal. This table compares three years at Bluehost and at hosting.com. It is our own arithmetic from each host's prices, using the 12-month offer and then the quoted renewal, against the longest term.

Host and plan1-year deal, then renewals for 3 yearsLongest term, scaled to 3 yearsDifference over 3 years
Bluehost Starter$381.84 ($50.88, then 24 months at $13.79)$143.64 (36 months at $3.99)$238.20 less
hosting.com Starter$353.64 ($17.88, then 24 months at $13.99)$71.64 (36 of 48 months at $1.99)$282.00 less

The long term wins on cost, but it needs the full payment up front and a plan you are sure about. The 30-day money-back guarantee is your test window. If you are not sure you will keep the site, take the shorter term.

Do you need a coupon code for Black Friday hosting deals?

Mostly no. Hostinger says Black Friday discounts are included in the order and no code is needed. Hosting.com applies its deal automatically. Kinsta's offer page shows no code for the first month free. Cloudways is the exception: it needs code BFCM802 at checkout on a new account. Bluehost's Buy More Save More offer also applies automatically at checkout, at 15% off one product, 20% off two or 25% off three or more, on the first 12-month term only.

Which hosts have no Black Friday hosting sale?

Some hosts do not run a sale, and some pages still show last year's offer. We found these:

  • BigScoots says on its own blog that it does not run Black Friday or Cyber Monday sales. It offers one-time discounts off the first bill instead.
  • Nexcess shows its managed WordPress plans from $19 a month with no sale on the plan page. Its parent, Liquid Web, has a Black Friday page whose text still showed 2025 dates when we read it on 15 November, so we did not list its prices.
  • DigitalOcean showed no Black Friday offer. A DigitalOcean community answer says new accounts get a $5 credit for 90 days.
  • Network Solutions lists code SITEWIDE30 for 30% off an AI All-Access Pack from 23 November to 7 December, but we found no hosting deal.

Is Black Friday a good time to buy web hosting?

It can be, if the deal lowers a price you would pay anyway. Prices move all year, and several hosts show a sale price on other dates too. Black Friday discounts apply to the first term only. Bluehost renews at the regular rate, Hostinger renews at $10.99, and hosting.com says its discounts apply to the first billing term only. Buy because the plan fits your site, then check the price you will pay in year two.

Can existing customers get Black Friday hosting deals?

It depends on the host. Kinsta's first month free and Cloudways' code are for new customers. Hostinger says you can claim its deal when you upgrade from hPanel. Bluehost's Buy More Save More applies to items in the same order. Ask the host's chat before you buy if you already have an account.

Eight checks before you pay

  1. Read the term. A 48-month price needs a 48-month payment, often up front.
  2. Read the renewal price. Put it in your calendar.
  3. Check who qualifies. Kinsta and Cloudways limit offers to new customers or new accounts, and ScalaHosting to new plans.
  4. Check the end date. Some pages disagree, as hosting.com's do.
  5. Check the freebies. A free domain or free email for the first year is not free for life. Ask what it costs in year two.
  6. Check the money-back guarantee. The hosts here list 30 days. Read what it covers: Bluehost, for example, deducts the domain fee from a refund.
  7. Check migration. Hostinger, hosting.com, Kinsta and Nexcess list free or assisted migration.
  8. Test before you move a live site. Copy the site, test it, check that support answers, then switch.

Our interest in this topic

Reinforce Lab builds and maintains WordPress sites. We may earn a commission when you buy hosting through the links on this page. We do not host sites ourselves. We list offers as hosts state them and say when we did not test something.

Final thoughts

Pick the host for the site you have, then check the price you will pay in year two. If a Black Friday offer fits, buy it before it ends. If it does not, wait. Hosting prices move all year. For a full comparison of 14 hosts, read our best web hosting services page.
